title: Design consistency audit of a stylesheet
when: The design looks slightly off everywhere and the user wants inconsistent colors, sizes, spacing and radii found and unified.
inputs: the main pages to check after changes
prompt:
Goal: An inventory of every distinct design value in the CSS, reduced to a small token set, with the replacements applied.
Steps:
1. Search the stylesheets per property family: color and background, font-size, margin, padding and gap, border-radius, box-shadow, z-index.
2. Count distinct values per family and how often each appears (for example 14 grays, 9 font sizes).
3. Cluster near duplicates: #333, #343434 and #2f2f2f become one; 15 px and 16 px become 1rem.
4. Define or reuse tokens for the survivors and replace every literal with var(); comment any value that is truly unique.
5. Compare components of one kind: buttons, inputs and cards share height, radius and padding.
6. Report before and after counts per family.
Quality bar:
- Each family ends small: about 8 colors, 6 to 8 sizes, 8 spacing steps, 3 radii, 4 shadows.
- No visual regression on the main pages.
- Contrast still passes after merging grays.
Pitfalls:
- Merging colors that carry meaning, such as danger red into brand red.
- Changing only half the files.
- Leaving old literals beside the new tokens.
Verify:
- [ ] Before and after counts reported.
- [ ] Literals replaced by var() references.
- [ ] Tokens on :root.
- [ ] Contrast passes.
Output: Updated stylesheets plus an audit table (family, before, after) in the reply.

examples.input: everything looks slightly different on each page, unify it
examples.output: grays 14 to 6, font sizes 11 to 7, radii 5 to 3, all as tokens
